answer.explanation: Replay fails at the first '⌊' token, the residue of the IPA markup ⌊λ…λ⌋. The tagger gave it the non-generic type n_-_pn_le, but the lexicon has no entry spelled '⌊' and n_-_pn_le has no generic entry, so lookup fails with 'missing lexical entry'. Every later '⌊' token (after 'fricative', 'друг', 'Бог', 'лёгкий', 'мягкий') has the same label and would fail the same way. Such unknown or markup tokens are handled by the ERG's generic entries, as 'Бог' already is with n_-_pn-gen_le.
answer.fix: Relabel all six '⌊' tokens with a generic type that the token's POS tag licenses: generic_proper_ne n_-_pn-gen_le (keeping n_sg_ilr and the hdn_bnp-pn_c / appositive / compound structure as proposed), or the generic quoted noun n_-_gq_le. No change to the grammar is needed.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the lexical leaf for "⌊/John": the lexicon has no n_-_pn_le entry with this spelling, so the proposed type finds no entry. No generic entry exists for n_-_pn_le either; the generic proper-noun type is n_-_pn-gen_le. The italicized "⌊/John loves a bagel/⌋" is cited material. The ERG normally analyzes it as a foreign/quoted word sequence of generic quoted nouns, not as a finite clause complementing "sentence". The tagger's lower-ranked tree labels for "loves" and "a" (w-w_fw-seq-m_c, w-w_fw-seq-t_c) point to this analysis.
answer.fix: Relabel the four cited words as generic quoted nouns: "⌊/John" as n_-_gq_le with w_italleft_plr, "loves" as n_-_gq_le, "a" as n_-_gq_le, and "bagel/⌋" as n_-_gq_le with w_italright_plr. Combine them with w-w_fw-seq-m_c / w-w_fw-seq-t_c and w_fw_c into a quoted NP. Attach that NP to "sentence" as an appositive or compound (e.g. hdn-np_app-r_c, mirroring the "the unit ⌊/loves/⌋" analysis later in the sentence) instead of the hd-cmp_u_c + sb-hd_nmc_c clause. Change "sentence" from n_cp_c-optc_le to a plain count noun if needed.

answer.explanation: The failure is subject-verb agreement in sb-hd_nmc_c. The subject was built as a full NP coordination (np-np_crd-t_c over two hdn_bnp-pn_c NPs), and NP-level 'and' coordination is plural (PN 3p). The verb 'makes' (v_3s-fin_olr) requires a 3s subject, so 3p & 3s fails. 'Johnson and Johnson' here names a single company, so the subject must be singular.
answer.fix: Coordinate below the NP level so the conjoined proper name stays singular. Change the tree labels of both 'Johnson' tokens from 'n_-_pn_le|n_sg_ilr|hdn_bnp-pn_c' to 'n_-_pn_le|n_sg_ilr|'. Join them with nominal coordination (n-n_crd-t_c, with 'and' under the nominal marker rule) and apply a single hdn_bnp-pn_c (or hdn_bnp_c) above the coordinated nominal. If the ERG's N-bar coordination also forces plural agreement, the cause is instead a missing construction: a singular name-compound coordination for company names like 'Johnson and Johnson'.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at lexical lookup, before any unification: there is no v_np_le entry for "preloaded" (stem "preload"), and the lexicon has no entry of any type under this spelling. v_np_le has no generic entry; the generic transitive-verb entries are v_np*_le (generic_trans_verb_*), licensed by the token's POS tag. So the tagger chose a non-generic type for an unknown word, and the prefix analysis (v_v-pre_dlr over a v_np_le stem) did not map to an existing entry. The ERG can still treat "preloaded" as an attributive passive participle through the generic verb or generic adjective route.
answer.fix: Relabel "preloaded" as v_np*_le|v_j-nb-pas-tr_dlr v_pas_odlr| (generic transitive verb, licensed by its VBN tag), keeping aj-hdn_norm_c above it. Alternatively, use the actual lexical type of the stem "load" with v_v-pre_dlr, or the generic adjective aj_-_i-unk_le. Leave the other labels unchanged.

answer.explanation: The failure is a lexical lookup, not a unification clash: the ERG has no lexical entry of type pt_-_sqright_le for a free-standing "'" token. Right quotes are attached to words as punctuation affixes during token mapping. As separate tokens, "'" only has the possessive clitic entries (n_-_cl-poss-pl_le, n_-_cl-poss-pr_le) and the feet-measure entry (n_-_c-meas-nocnh_le). The apostrophe in "Rus'" belongs to the name itself, but the grammar's preprocessing split it off as if it were a plural possessive. None of the available readings fits, because no possessed noun follows it ('Kievan Rus' in about 880').
answer.fix: Keep "Rus'" as a single token so it can be a generic proper name (n_-_pn-gen_le with n_sg_ilr), either through a token-mapping or REPP exception or by handling the apostrophe as RPUNCT on "Rus". Also relabel "Rus" with n_sg_ilr instead of n_pl_olr.

answer.explanation: Root_strict requires SYNSEM.LOCAL.CAT.MC +, but the clause it receives is MC na. 'Please' (av_-_dc-pls_le) copies its modifiee's MC to the mother through #mc, so the na must come from the subject-auxiliary-inverted clause built on v_aux-sb-inv_dlr. Most likely, inverted polar questions are not accepted as strict main clauses without question-mark punctuation, and this one ends in a period, so the input is an informally punctuated question.
answer.fix: No change to the lexical tags. Treat this as robust input: accept the item under a robust or informal root (for example root_informal), or normalise the final '.' to '?'. If questions ending in a period should be admitted, let the period path or the root license MC na inverted clauses.

answer.explanation: "Multivariate" is not in the ERG lexicon, so Orca used the generic entry generic_adj (aj_-_i-unk_le). That entry requires the token's POS tag TOKENS.+LIST.FIRST.+TNT.+TAGS.FIRST to be "JJ", but the token carries "GQ", and the two do not unify. The rest of the derivation is also mis-shaped: aj-hdn_norm_c sits at the very top, so the adjective modifies the whole root clause instead of the noun "regression".
answer.fix: Give the token "Multivariate" the POS tag JJ so generic_adj (aj_-_i-unk_le) is licensed. Attach it inside the subject: aj-hdn_norm_c(Multivariate, regression), then the bare-NP rule (hdn_bnp_c), then the parenthetical "(above)" via hdn-cl_prnth_c. The sentence root (root_strict over sb-hd_mc_c) should be the top node. Also check the label for "above": an adverb or preposition is likely better than n_-_m-ncmp-nttl_le.

answer.explanation: Lexical lookup fails at the leaf for "connotative". The ERG lexicon has no native entry for this spelling, and aj_-_i_le is not a generic type, so Orca finds no entry of the proposed type. Unknown adjectives are handled by the generic entry generic_adj of type aj_-_i-unk_le, licensed by a JJ tag in +TNT.+TAGS, so this is a tagging error, not a gap in the grammar.
answer.fix: Relabel "connotative" as aj_-_i-unk_le (generic_adj) and keep aj-hdn_norm_c above it. Check "denotative" too: if it is also absent from the lexicon, it needs aj_-_i-unk_le in place of aj_-_i_le.

answer.explanation: At cl-rc_c (the VP-final relative clause), the second daughter must have a HEAD.MOD of type synsem. Here that daughter is the main-clause wh-question 'which are the cheapest' (flr-hd_wh-mc-sb_c), whose MOD is anti_synsem, so unification fails. The bracketing is wrong: the relative clause 'you have on hand' (have with its NP complement extracted, 'on hand' as the predicative complement) should end at 'hand,'. The whole fronted PP 'Of the items you have on hand,' should then attach to the main question clause 'which are the cheapest?'. It should not be glued inside the relative clause.
answer.fix: Remove cl-rc_c above 'have'. Make node 0.1.1.1.0.1 just the VP hd-cmp_u_c(hd_xcmp_c(have), on hand), so the relative clause is cl_rc-fin-nwh_c(sb-hd_nmc_c(you, have on hand)) with the comma on 'hand'. At the top, combine the PP 'Of … hand,' with the clause flr-hd_wh-mc-sb_c('which', 'are the cheapest?') as a scopal pre-head adjunct (aj-hd_scp_c, which the tagger offered for the comma). If needed, relabel 'Of' as a modifier preposition rather than p_np_ptcl-of_le.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the lexical leaf for "minidisc": the tagger chose n_-_c_le, but the ERG lexicon has no entry for this spelling, and n_-_c_le has no generic (unknown-word) entry, so no lexical entry can be built. The grammar handles unknown common nouns through its generic entries in gle.tdl, so this is a tagging error, not a gap in the grammar. Separately, the proposed tree is malformed: "What" attaches by sp-hd_n_c above the whole root clause, when it should be the specifier of "kind of minidisc players" inside the wh-filler.
answer.fix: Relabel "minidisc" as the generic mass/count noun n_-_mc-unk_le (generic_mass_count_noun, licensed by its NN tag), keeping hdn_bnp_c above the compound n-hdn_cpd_c. Make "What" (d_-_wh_le) combine by sp-hd_n_c with "kind of minidisc players", and use the resulting NP as the filler of flr-hd_wh-mc_c under root_strict. Also check that "players" resolves to an existing entry for "player" with n_pl_olr (probably n_-_c_le if n_pp_c-of_le has no entry).

answer.explanation: At hd-aj_vmod_c, the rule that attaches a following intersective adjunct to a verb with an NP complement already in place, the adjunct's MOD..VAL.SUBJ.FIRST.OPT value clashes (- vs +) with what the rule and the head 'Inform me' supply. The discourse 'please' (av_-_dc-pls_le) is meant for clause-level uses such as 'Please leave.' and is incompatible with this mid-VP post-head attachment. The lexicon also lists 'please' as a post-head VP modifier (av_-_i-vp-po-nmb_le), which should fit 'Inform me please whether ...'.
answer.fix: Relabel 'please' from av_-_dc-pls_le to av_-_i-vp-po-nmb_le (the tagger's third choice) and keep the hd-aj_vmod_c attachment. 'Inform' as v_np-cp_le or v_np-cp_fin-inf_le should then take the whether-clause as its complement.

answer.explanation: hdn-n_prnth_c (paren_float_nbar_rule) requires its nominal head daughter to have an empty COMPS list. Here 'implementations' (n_pp_mc-of_le + n_pl_olr) still has its of-PP complement on COMPS, because the derivation saturates that complement only later, with hd-cmp_u_c above the parenthetical. So COMPS *null* clashes with *cons*. The grammar can still analyze the phrase: the noun closes its optional complement first, and 'of the character encoding…' attaches as a post-nominal PP modifier after the parenthetical.
answer.fix: Label 'implementations' as n_pp_mc-of_le|n_pl_olr|hdn_optcmp_c (the tagger's second choice). Label 'of' as p_np_i-nm-poss_le (also its second choice), attached by hdn-aj_redrel_c to the N-bar 'implementations (especially old ones)' instead of by hd-cmp_u_c. Separately, the later VP structure is also mis-tagged and needs fixing: 'and do not include…' should coordinate with 'are aimed…' through vp-vp_crd-fin-t_c at the top VP, and should not sit inside the NP 'simultaneous use…'.

answer.explanation: Replay fails before any unification: the lexicon has no entry of any type for the straight ASCII quote ", and pt_-_dqleft_le has no generic entry, so lookup gives 'missing lexical entry'. In the ERG, straight double quotes are normally not separate lexical items. Token mapping attaches them to the adjacent word, and punctuation lexical rules license them there, so analysing " as a standalone pt_-_dqleft_le leaf (and the right quote as a pt_-_dqright_le leaf under hd-pct_c) is a labelling error.
answer.fix: Drop the standalone quote leaves and their pct-hd_c and hd-pct_c nodes. Label "out" as pp_-_i_le with the left-double-quote punctuation rule (w_dqleft_plr or the equivalent quote prefix rule). Label "there" as n_-_ad-acc_le with the right-double-quote punctuation rule (w_dqright_plr) before np_adv_c and hdn_bnp-qnt_c. The rest of the derivation stays as proposed.

answer.explanation: The ERG preprocessing removed the opening link mark '⌊>' but left the closing '>⌋' inside the word, producing the token 'India>⌋n' instead of 'Indian'. No lexical entry of type aj_-_i-cap_le matches the spelling 'India>⌋n', and aj_-_i-cap_le has no generic entry, so lookup fails with 'missing lexical entry'. The tagger's choice of a capitalized intersective adjective is right for 'Indian'; the lexical entry exists, but the token never reaches it.
answer.fix: Extend the link-mark rule in gml.rpp so that a closing '>⌋' followed by any word-internal suffix is removed, not just the plural 's'. This turns '⌊>India>⌋n' into 'Indian', which then matches its existing aj_-_i-cap_le entry. Without changing the preprocessor, the only workaround is to retag the token as a generic proper noun (n_-_pn-gen_le with n_sg_ilr and hdn_bnp-pn_c) in an np-hdn_cpd_c compound with 'views'.

answer.explanation: At node 0.0.0.0, hdn-aj_redrel_c (hadj_i_redrel_npr_rule) requires its non-head daughter to have HEAD n_or_a_or_p_or_adv. That rule is for postnominal predicative APs and PPs. Here the daughter is vp_rc-redrel_c, built over the passive verb 'needed' (v_pas_odlr), so its HEAD is verb, and verb does not unify with n_or_a_or_p_or_adv. A reduced relative from a passive VP should attach with the ordinary head-relative-clause rule instead.
answer.fix: Relabel node 0.0.0.0 as hdn-aj_rc_c instead of hdn-aj_redrel_c, keeping vp_rc-redrel_c over 'needed.' (the tagger's third tree label for Thinkpad, 'hdn_bnp_c hdn-aj_rc_c'). If hdn_bnp-pn_c then fails over the modified nominal, also change the bare-NP rule above it to hdn_bnp_c. Lexical labels can stay as tagged (IBM may preferably be n_-_pn-upcase_le, its lexicon type).

answer.explanation: Replay fails because there is no lexical entry for the ASCII straight quote '"'. The type pt_-_dqleft_le is the right analysis for a left quote. The problem is the spelling: the ERG's left- and right-quote entries (pt_-_dqleft_le, pt_-_dqright_le) are keyed on the directional characters “ and ”, and the ERG's preprocessing normally rewrites a straight quote into one of them by context. Here the token stayed '"', so the lookup failed; the closing quote (pt_-_dqright_le) would fail the same way.
answer.fix: Normalize straight double quotes in tokenization before lookup, as the ERG preprocessing does: rewrite the opening '"' before 'tossicomania' as “ and the closing one as ”. Keep the tagger's labels pt_-_dqleft_le and pt_-_dqright_le. Alternatively, make Orca's lookup map '"' to the dqleft or dqright entry according to the proposed type.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf for "minima" because no lexical entry exists for the type aj_-_i-crd-one_le, the one-digit cardinal adjective used for words like 'eight', and that type has no generic entry. "minima" is not in the ERG lexicon at all, so it can only be covered by a generic unknown-word entry. The tagger instead chose a closed-class numeral type, together with the matching unary rule hdn_np-num_c, which is simply the wrong category for this word. As the plural of 'minimum', it should be the generic plural noun, which the POS tag NNS licenses, and the bare NP 'local minima' then builds as usual.
answer.fix: Relabel "minima" as n_-_c-pl-unk_le (generic_pl_noun) with no lexical rules, and drop hdn_np-num_c. The parent structure stays the same: aj-hdn_norm_c(local, minima) under hdn_bnp_c. Optionally, add minimum_n1's irregular plural 'minima' to irregs.tab so the native noun entry is found.

answer.explanation: The failure is at the lexical lookup, not at unification. The token "⌊/reduced/⌋" has no entry in the lexicon, and its proposed type v_np*_le (passive participle via v_pas_odlr and v_j-nme-tr_dlr) has no generic entry that applies here. The generic transitive-verb entries are licensed only by a verbal POS tag, and this italicized cited word carries markup on both sides. Following the ERG's GML conventions, italicized cited material should be a generic quoted noun (n_-_gq_le, entry generic_quoted) with the italics rules, parallel to "⌊/ultra-short/⌋" in the same coordination.
answer.fix: Relabel "⌊/reduced/⌋" as n_-_gq_le|w_italright_plr w_italleft_plr| (the tagger's second-ranked kind of label), heading a bare NP (hdn_bnp-pn_c). It then serves as the NP conjunct of "or", or as an adjunct to the following IPA noun via aj-hdn_norm_c. The structure above it may need to be re-derived; the mangled IPA tokens "⌊" should keep n_-_pn_le|n_sg_ilr with hd-pct_nobrk_c.

answer.explanation: Replay failed at the leaf for "Availability" because the lexicon has no n_-_m_le entry for this spelling, only n_-_mc_le (mass/count noun), and n_-_m_le has no generic entry. The grammar can analyze the sentence as a bare-NP fragment with "of desktop computers" as a post-nominal PP, provided the head noun uses its actual lexical type.
answer.fix: Relabel "Availability" as n_-_mc_le with the mass inflection rule (n_-_mc_le|n_ms-cnt_ilr| or the appropriate mass reading for mc nouns), keeping the tree label root_inffrag np_frg_c hdn_bnp_c hdn-aj_redrel_c; the other labels can stay.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf pt_-_dqleft_le for the token ", with 'missing lexical entry'. The ERG's quote-mark entries (pt_-_dqleft_le and pt_-_dqright_le) are spelled with the directional quotes “ and ”, and the lexicon has no entry at all for the straight ASCII quote. The tagger's types for both quote marks (dqleft for the opening one, dqright for the closing one) are correct. The problem is that the token reached lexical lookup as an undirected ASCII " instead of being normalized to “ or ” by preprocessing.
answer.fix: Normalize straight double quotes to directional ones before lexical lookup: the opening " before 'context' becomes “ and the closing one becomes ”. This can be done in REPP or token mapping, or in Orca's lookup. Alternatively, add ASCII-" orthographies to the pt_-_dqleft_le and pt_-_dqright_le punctuation entries. No change to the tagger's labels is needed for this failure.

answer.explanation: The failure is at the leaf for "kinda". The tagger chose aj_-_i-unk_le, which forced the generic entry generic_adj. That entry requires the token's POS tag to be JJ (TOKENS.+LIST.FIRST.+TNT.+TAGS.FIRST "JJ"), but this token carries "GQ", so the two do not unify. In any case "kinda" is a known word (av_-_dg-v_le and n_nb_c_le), so no generic entry should have been used; the tagger's second-best labels (n_nb_c_le with n_sg_ilr, attached by n-hdn_cpd_c) select the lexicon's nominal entry.
answer.fix: Relabel "kinda" as n_nb_c_le|n_sg_ilr| and replace aj-hdn_norm_c over "kinda phones" with n-hdn_cpd_c, which the tagger ranked second. Keep the rest of the derivation (what + N' via sp-hd_n_c, topicalized NP filler, sb-hd_nmc_c with extracted complement of "got").

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf for "GB" because the lexicon has no entry of type n_-_c-meas-abb_le with that spelling, and that type has no generic entry. The tagger's choice matches the parallel "256 MB", where MB is an abbreviated measure noun that num-n_mnp_c combines with a cardinal. GB exists only as n_-_pn_le and n_pp_c-of_le, which do not give the measure-noun analysis that "30 GB hard drive" needs, so this is a gap in the lexicon rather than a tagging error.
answer.fix: Add a lexical entry for "GB" (gigabyte) of type n_-_c-meas-abb_le, parallel to the existing MB entry, with the same predicate pattern as MB (e.g. _gigabyte_n_1).

answer.explanation: np-np_crd-nc-m_c coordinates NPs, so its second daughter must be a saturated NP. Here it is the N-bar built by hdn_color_c over "green ) .", and that N-bar still has a non-optional specifier requirement (SPR.FIRST.OPT -). This clashes with the OPT + the rule requires, unlike "red" and "blue", which were wrapped in hdn_bnp_c. The analysis the grammar can build is the same one the tagger already ranked highly for the other conjuncts: color noun, then bare NP, then punctuation.
answer.fix: Change the tree label of "green" from '2|hd-pct_c' to 'N|hdn_bnp_c hdn_color_c hd-pct_c', so that "green" gets hdn_color_c and then hdn_bnp_c before it enters the coordination. Attach the ")" with hd-pct_c above the bare NP, or above the whole parenthetical PP. Also attach the final "." at the top level, to the whole clause, rather than inside the parenthesis on "green".

answer.explanation: Preprocessing has collapsed the whole IPA span ⌊λ…λ⌋ into one token shown as "⌊". The tagger labelled it n_-_pn_le, but that type has no generic entry and the lexicon has no entry for this spelling, so replay fails with "missing lexical entry" before any unification. The ERG's generic unknown-word entries cover this case (a proper-name or quoted-material generic), and the rest of the derivation is plausible, so this is a labelling error rather than a grammar gap.
answer.fix: Relabel the token "⌊" with a generic type that has a gle.tdl entry and whose POS tag matches: n_-_pn-gen_le (generic_proper_ne) with n_sg_ilr, keeping hdn_bnp-pn_c and hd-pct_nobrk_c above it. The alternative is n_-_gq_le (generic_quoted), with hdn_bnp_c in place of hdn_bnp-pn_c. All other labels stay unchanged.

answer.explanation: hd_yesno_c requires its daughter to be an inverted clause (HEAD.INV +). The proposed tree instead uses non-inverted main verb 'do' (v_np-np_only_le via v_n3s-bse_ilr, INV -) taking 'you' and a bare NP 'stock' as two objects, so INV + fails to unify with INV -. The correct analysis is auxiliary 'do' (v_vp_do-f_le + v_aux-sb-inv_dlr), subject 'you', and a bare VP 'stock'. But the lexicon has 'stock' only as v_np_le (obligatory object), v_p_le and v_p-pp_le, plus the noun. With no intransitive or optional-object verb entry, the VP 'stock' cannot be built.
answer.fix: Add an optional-object verb entry for 'stock' (type v_np*_le, e.g. stock_v2 alongside stock_v1). Then tag 'Do' as v_vp_do-f_le|v_aux-sb-inv_dlr and 'stock' as v_np*_le|v_n3s-bse_ilr with hd_optcmp_c. If the input is instead a truncated 'Do you stock X?', treat it as ungrammatical or robust input.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf pt_-_dqleft_le for the token "\"". The ERG lexicon has no entry with the ASCII double-quote spelling, and pt_-_dqleft_le has no generic entry, so lexical lookup fails before any unification takes place. The tag itself is correct; most likely the preprocessing should have rewritten the straight quotes to the typographic left and right quotes that the lexicon's quote entries spell (the ( and " sequence with no space before the quote probably blocked the context-sensitive REPP quote rule). The same preprocessing also mangled the GML emphasis markup, leaving the stray token 'ц∗⌋апля' with its opening mark removed.
answer.fix: Fix tokenization/REPP so that ASCII double quotes next to parentheses are normalized to left and right typographic quotes (the left quote mapped to pt_-_dqleft_le, the right to pt_-_dqright_le). Also make the GML rules handle intra-word emphasis ⌊∗ц∗⌋апля, so that the word is a single clean token such as 'цапля' or a generic quoted noun (n_-_gq_le). Keep the proposed lexical types.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the left-quote leaf: there is no lexical entry of type pt_-_dqleft_le with the spelling '"', and the lexicon has no entry of any type for that spelling. The tagger's type is right: the quote opens the quoted fragment and attaches by pct-hd_c. The ERG's left and right double-quote entries are keyed to the directional quote characters, which preprocessing normally produces from straight quotes. Here the straight ASCII quote reached lookup unchanged, so neither the opening nor the closing '"' (dqright, after the period) can be found.
answer.fix: Normalise the straight '"' tokens to the ERG's left and right quote characters before lexical lookup, matching the ERG's REPP or token-mapping conventions; this is the opening quote before 'Because' and the closing quote after '.'. The tags pt_-_dqleft_le and pt_-_dqright_le should then find entries. Alternatively, add ASCII-spelled pt_-_dqleft_le and pt_-_dqright_le entries.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the lexical lookup for the token "do.", which was tagged aj_-_i-nopn_le: no adjective entry exists for "do", and that type has no generic entry. The token is the verb "do" ('suffice', as in "this will do") with its period attached. That period should be stripped by the punctuation lexical rule w_period_plr, and the verb must be in base form to be the VP complement of v_vp_will-p_le. The tagger's third-ranked label already has this shape.
answer.fix: Retag "do." as the intransitive verb lexeme for do, using the type of the lexicon's intransitive 'suffice' entry (the tagger proposes v_-_unacc_le), with lexical rules w_period_plr and v_n3s-bse_ilr, so that hd-cmp_u_c combines "will" with the base-form VP. Keep the three '?' tokens as pt_-_qmark_le attached by hd-pct_c. If the stacked punctuation still fails, the sentence would fall under punctuation or robust input instead.

answer.explanation: The failure is at 'res', which has no native lexicon entry, so Orca fell back to generic_pl_noun (n_-_c-pl-unk_le). That entry requires the token's first POS tag to be "NNS" (TOKENS.+LIST.FIRST.+TNT.+TAGS.FIRST), but preprocessing tagged this token "GQ", the tag that licenses the generic quoted-noun entry. The plural-unknown-noun label is therefore incompatible with the token, and it is a tagging error, not a gap in the grammar.
answer.fix: Relabel 'res' with a generic type its GQ tag licenses, most likely n_-_gq_le (generic_quoted). Keep it as the head of the aj-hdn_norm_c with 'high-' inside the noun compound, and adjust the unary rule above it if needed (e.g. hdn_bnp_c over the n-hdn_cpd_c).

answer.explanation: At 0.0.1.1.0.0.1.0.1 the rule sp-hd_hc_c combines 'less' as a specifier with 'often'. 'often' is tagged av_-_i-vp-x_le, whose SPR wants a specifier with MINORS.MIN adv_rel. The degree specifier av_-_dg-cmp-less_le has MIN compos_spec_rel, so the two clash. This x-type entry of 'often' does not take comparative degree specifiers, while another entry of 'often' does, so the grammar has a path for 'less often'. The tree above is also implausible: a second sp-hd_hc_c makes 'less often' the specifier of the proper NP 'German'. The intended reading is an elliptical parenthetical, 'French (and) less often German', not a specified noun.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf for "cures" because the ERG has no entry of type v_-_unacc_le for the stem "cure". The verb is listed only as transitive (cure_v1, a v_np*_le-style entry with an optional object), and v_-_unacc_le has no generic entry to fall back on. Intransitive "the new concrete cures faster" can still be analyzed as the transitive entry with its optional object discharged, which is the tagger's second-best label.
answer.fix: Relabel "cures" as v_np*_le with v_3s-fin_olr and unary hd_optcmp_c, keeping hd-aj_scp_c above it. Separately, an intransitive or unaccusative entry for cure (as in concrete or resin curing) would be a reasonable addition to the lexicon. Further down, "Materials Today" should probably be one proper name rather than an apposition plus an np_adv_c adverb.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the lexical leaf for "creaky". The tagger chose aj_-_i-er_le, but the ERG lexicon has no entry for "creaky" of any type, and aj_-_i-er_le has no generic (gle.tdl) entry, so lookup returns "missing lexical entry". Unknown adjectives are meant to go through the generic adjective generic_adj (aj_-_i-unk_le), licensed by a JJ POS tag; the tagger ranked this type second (0.231).
answer.fix: Relabel "creaky" as aj_-_i-unk_le with no lexical rules, keeping the hd-pct_c attachment. This needs the token to carry a JJ tag in +TNT.+TAGS. Leave the rest of the derivation unchanged. If replay then fails elsewhere, the next thing to check is the mixed commas: pt_-_comma-informal_le after "old" versus pt_-_comma_le after "creaky".

answer.explanation: 'lanolin' is not in the lexicon, so it can only enter through a generic entry for the tagger's type n_-_mc-unk_le. The reported failure is generic_mass_noun's constraint TOKENS.+LIST.FIRST.+TNT.+TAGS.FIRST "FW", which clashes with the token's tag "GQ". A POS tag of GQ (the quoted-material tag) is wrong for a plain common noun, which should carry NN and license generic_mass_count_noun. The lexical type label and the rest of the derivation look plausible, so the problem is the token's POS tag during replay, not the grammar.
answer.fix: Give the token 'lanolin' a POS tag of NN, not GQ, in the replay input (or have Orca pick the generic entry whose tag constraint matches), so that generic_mass_count_noun (n_-_mc-unk_le) is used. Keep the label n_-_mc-unk_le|n_ms-cnt_ilr; no change to the grammar is needed.

answer.explanation: The generic entry generic_pl_noun (n_-_c-pl-unk_le) requires the token's POS tag to be NNS (TOKENS.+LIST.FIRST.+TNT.+TAGS.FIRST "NNS"). Preprocessing tagged 'lederhosen' as GQ, which marks quoted or italicized foreign material, so the unification fails. 'lederhosen' has no native lexical entry, and the only generic entry the GQ tag licenses is the generic quoted noun (generic_quoted, n_-_gq_le).
answer.fix: Relabel 'lederhosen' as n_-_gq_le|| (generic_quoted), keeping sp-hd_n_c with 'His' and the rest of the tree unchanged. If the text was not italicized, the alternative is to retag the token NNS so that generic_pl_noun applies.

answer.explanation: Replay fails at the leaf for "overproof". The tagger chose n_-_c-nocnh_le, but the word is not in the lexicon and that type has no generic entry, so lexical lookup fails before any unification. Here "overproof" is a bare-infinitive verb, the VP complement of causative "let" ("letting the sourdough overproof"), so the noun reading and the attachment built on it are wrong.
answer.fix: Retag "overproof" as the generic bare-form verb v_np*_le (generic_trans_verb_bse, with v_n3s-bse_ilr, optional object unexpressed). Retag "letting" from v_np_ntr_le to the NP+VP(bse) causative type (v_np-vp_bse_le + v_prp_olr). Retag "sourdough" as the generic noun n_-_mc-unk_le + n_ms-cnt_ilr, heading the NP "the sourdough" with sp-hd_n_c. Re-derive the structure above these words: the comma and quote attach to the clause, not to a noun.

answer.fix: Relabel "hi" as n_-_pn-abb_le|n_sg_ilr|hdn_bnp-pn_c, keeping the hyphen compound with "-" as pt_-_hyphn-rgt_le. Give the unknown "vis" a generic type its POS tag licenses (e.g. n_-_mc-unk_le or aj_-_i-unk_le) rather than folding it into the hyphen token. Rebuild the top of the tree so that [Wearing ... clipboard,] is a vp_sbrd-pre_c modifier of the main clause sb-hd_mc_c "the intern wandered the warehouse" (wandered as v_np*_le or v_pp*_dir_le taking "the warehouse"), with the "scanning ... wondering ..." participial VPs as a post-head subordinate modifier.

The lexicon lists "tide" only as n_pp_c-of_le, a count noun with an optional of-PP complement, and n_-_c_le has no generic entry for unknown words to fall back on. Insert hdn_optcmp_c above it to discharge the optional complement, so the path is hd-pct_c > hdn_optcmp_c > n_sg_ilr, or hdn_optcmp_c over hd-pct_c (the tagger's second-best tree label). answer.explanation: vp_rc-redrel_c builds a reduced relative from a verbal (participial) VP, so its daughter's HEAD must be verb. Here "closed" was tagged as the adjective aj_-_i_le, which gives the conflict HEAD verb & adj. The participle reading of "close" (passive of v_np_noger_le, the tagger's second choice) is available, and the rest of the derivation is also badly mis-structured: "bridge," plus the relative is built with sb-hd_mc_c, "new" is tagged as a noun, "steels" as a finite verb, and "any previously installed" is built with sb-hd_nmc_c.
answer.fix: Tag "closed" as v_np_noger_le|v_pas_odlr|hd_optcmp_c, so that vp_rc-redrel_c (or the adjective with hdn-aj_redrel_c) attaches as a postnominal modifier of "bridge," via hdn-aj_rc_c / hdn-aj_redrel_c instead of sb-hd_mc_c. Downstream, make these changes: "new" -> aj_-_i_le (aj-hdn_norm_c); "steels" -> n_-_mc_le|n_pl_olr; "used" and "installed" -> passive participles (v_pas_odlr) as reduced relatives attached by hdn-aj_redrel_c to "steels" and to "any" (not sb-hd_nmc_c); "region" without the hd-pct_c analysis that attaches the period inside the NP.

answer.explanation: Replay failed at the leaf for the multi-token word 'heads - up' because the lexicon has no entry of type n_cp_c-optc_le with that orthography, and n_cp_c-optc_le has no generic entry to fall back on. Here 'heads-up' takes a finite that-clause complement ('a heads-up that the migration has been postponed'), like 'feeling' or 'notice'. A CP-complement noun type such as n_cp_c-optc_le is therefore the right analysis, so the tag itself is plausible. As far as I can tell, the ERG either lacks 'heads-up' entirely or has it only as a plain count noun. No other tagging would let the that-clause attach, which is consistent with no repair being found.
answer.fix: Add a lexical entry such as heads_up_n1 := n_cp_c-optc_le & [ ORTH < "heads", "-", "up" > ] (or the hyphenated single-token form the ERG's tokenization yields), with PRED _heads-up_n_1_rel. A plain n_-_c_le variant could be added as well.
